A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, renamed from InstaDrag to LightningDrag. All 13 pages of each, including equations, tables, qualitative figures and references, support comparison. Neither PDF contains a separately labeled appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original DragBench accuracy and timing results in Tables 1–2, alongside qualitative experiments and ablations in Figures 4–10.

after.justification: v2 retains these original quantitative results, qualitative experiments and ablations under the LightningDrag name.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.4 retain the same video-pair construction, inpainting backbone, appearance encoder, point embeddings, noise prior, guidance and dragging strategies. The method is renamed without a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both use the same internal video training data, DragBench evaluation and qualitative scenarios covering pose changes, scaling, translation, local deformation and multi-round dragging.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains DragGAN, DragDiffusion, DiffEditor, Readout Guidance and SDEDrag. Table 2 and Figure 8 retain the same four diffusion baselines; only the proposed method's name changes.

E3.justification: Both report 220k training samples, 205 DragBench evaluation samples and timing on 67 square images at 512 × 512 on an A100. Metrics, preprocessing, training settings, sampling steps and guidance settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The noise-prior and guidance-schedule comparisons in Figures 4–5, point augmentation in Figure 6, sequential dragging in Figure 7 and multi-round examples in Figure 10 are retained.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains the same timing uncertainty entries and reporting practice. No repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain every score and timing entry. The base method remains at IF 0.885, MD 18.62 and 2.06 ± 0.05 seconds; its LCM-LoRA variant remains at 0.890, 18.95 and 0.92 ± 0.02 seconds. Qualitative examples and findings also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 and the guidance-schedule definitions are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, propositions or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about conditional generation, learning editing from videos, speed, editing quality and generalization to local deformations. Renaming does not alter their scope.

C2.justification: Both retain the noise and guidance explanations, the interpretation of SDEDrag's high fidelity as sometimes reflecting identity mapping, and the Stable Diffusion V1.5 limitations concerning small details, hands and faces.

D1.justification: The project address changes from instadrag.github.io to lightning-drag.github.io, and the promised code/model repository changes from magic-research/InstaDrag to magic-research/LightningDrag. Technical details remain unchanged; both still say the code and model will be released.

R1.justification: The same 69 references and the same related-work positioning in Section 2 are retained. Bibliographic differences are limited to layout and pagination.

P1.justification: The title and method name change throughout from InstaDrag to LightningDrag, and the version header is updated. Section order and substantive prose remain unchanged, with local reflow around the longer name.

P2.justification: Figure 1's plots and figure/table labels and captions are updated for the new name, accompanied by small sizing, table-width and text-flow changes. The same ten figures and two tables remain.

improvement.justification: v2 primarily renames the method and updates resource addresses and presentation. The method, experimental evidence, claims and limitations remain unchanged. These edits establish no meaningful net improvement or deterioration in the paper's overall quality.
